answer: Latency triangulation costs each fake its own host (~$5/day): every epoch three random established peers send a 'sable' probe (a dark, unannounced ping) from different regions, and the round-trip times must put the agent on its own ledge of the latency map. Keys answering from one haven, same ledge within 2 ms, are merged into one seat. A farm can't share or bulk-rent one rack, since every alias needs a separate machine in a distinct place, so cost scales linearly per fake. Limit: VPN noise makes merges soft evidence.
